info.title: TickerInside API
info.summary: Holdings of 5,433 US ETFs, which ETFs hold a stock, and overlap, as static JSON.
info.description:
TickerInside is an open, machine-readable database of US ETF holdings, with the source and date of each holding. It serves the holdings of 5,433 US ETFs with their weights, which ETFs hold a stock and at what weight, and the overlap between any two stock ETFs. Static JSON, with no key or sign-up, and CORS open to any origin. The licence is CC BY 4.0: credit TickerInside with a link to the page the figure comes from wherever the medium allows a link, and by name where it does not; how you mark the link is up to you. It covers TickerInside's own contribution; the holdings in issuer files are facts as each issuer publishes them, so check the issuer's terms before bulk commercial reuse. The holdings history (/api/v1/history.json, /api/v1/history/) and the ETF flows computed from it (/api/v1/flows.json, /api/v1/flows.csv, /api/v1/flows/, /feeds/) have their own terms: https://tickerinside.com/legal/#history.

688 funds, the issuer layer, are read every weekday night from their issuers' own holdings files. 1,952 more, the SEC layer, are read from their latest SEC Form N-PORT filing, which is months older. 922 fixed income funds, 235 multi-asset funds and 1,365 derivative-based funds come from the same filings, and 131 trusts and pools from their own SEC filings. 140 funds from their sponsors' own files, too new for a Form N-PORT. Every fund file carries the date of its holdings. Where the price data has enough of a fund's or a stock's history, its file also carries its weekly returns over 156 weeks. The weeks are the same in every file, so any basket of them can be correlated. Each stock file also carries its line of the ETF ownership ledger: the share of the company's shares outstanding that the covered funds hold, at least, with the SEC's count and its date. The method is in https://tickerinside.com/api/v1/methods.json. The same data answers inside Claude, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP clients through the server at https://tickerinside.com/mcp.

layers.issuer_files: Read every weekday night from the issuer's own daily holdings file.
layers.sec_nport: A US stock ETF, from its latest public SEC Form N-PORT filing.
layers.sec_nport_derivatives: A leveraged, inverse, option income or other derivative-based ETF, from its latest SEC Form N-PORT filing: what it holds, and its swaps, futures and options as notional exposure.
layers.sec_nport_bonds: A fixed income ETF (bond, credit, mortgage, Treasury, municipal and the like), from its latest SEC Form N-PORT filing: its lines by issuer, coupon and maturity, and its weight by kind, maturity and country.
layers.sec_nport_multi_asset: A multi-asset ETF: a fund that holds other funds or several asset classes (allocation, target date, buffer, income and hedged strategies), from its latest SEC Form N-PORT filing.
layers.trust_filings: A trust or pool that files no Form N-PORT (physical metal, crypto, currency, commodity futures), from its own SEC filings.
layers.sponsor_files: A fund with no Form N-PORT yet, from the holdings its sponsor publishes on its own site, read every night by tickers only: the file's date and the sponsor's page are in the file.
layers.prospectus: A fund with no holdings file yet: what its prospectus states (its objective, its index or target, its cost). No holdings; its first holdings filing replaces the file.

reasons.etn: An exchange-traded note is a debt of the bank that issues it, not a fund, and holds nothing to list. Told from a fund by its name (ETN, ETNs, ETRACS, iPath, X-Links), unless the name also says ETF.
reasons.other_product: Not a fund: a trust certificate, which holds nothing to list. Told by its name.
reasons.no_filing_yet: The SEC lists the fund's ticker and it has filed no public Form N-PORT yet. A new fund files its first about two to five months after it lists.
reasons.not_in_sec_list: Not in the SEC's list of fund tickers yet, so it has no Form N-PORT to read. A new fund reaches that list after it lists.
reasons.other_fund: The SEC's ticker file still gives this ticker the series of another fund, and that series' newest filing is under the other fund's name, so the ETF's own holdings are not read from it. It joins when its own filing does.
reasons.stale_filing: The newest public Form N-PORT found for this ticker describes a portfolio more than nine months old, so it is not served as current holdings. It joins when a newer filing does.
reasons.no_prospectus_found: No holdings file yet, and no prospectus of the fund was found on EDGAR. It is looked up again every few days.

get.description: The holdings with their weights and the date of their source, then cost, returns, risk and weekly returns over 156 weeks where the data has them. A figure the data lacks is null, and so is a week without a return; with fewer than 110 weekly returns, weekly is an empty list, or null for a fund from SEC filings. This is the endpoint most things are built from. The funds no issuer file covers are served in the same shape from their latest SEC filing, with eight more fields: report_date, filed, filing_url, net_assets, multi_class, stock_pct, unmapped_pct and abroad. A fund of the other layers answers too, from its /etf/ file. The holdings map and the weekly series make this file enough on its own. The overlap of any two stock ETFs is a walk over two holdings maps, and a covariance matrix for any basket is a walk over their weekly series.

get.description: In this path sec stands for security, not the SEC: the file is one stock and the funds that hold it, and a fund's own holdings are in /api/v1/fund/{ticker}.json. Name, sector, market cap, valuation, returns, risk, the funds that hold it from issuer files and from SEC filings, and its weekly returns over the same 156 weeks as the fund files. Every stock in the price data with at least 110 weekly returns in those weeks has a file here, whether or not any covered fund holds it. A stock with fewer has one when a fund read from an issuer file or a stock ETF from SEC filings holds it in a file dated since it listed, the price data has its closes since its listing, or a year of them, the last at most five sessions old, and Nasdaq Trader's directory lists it under its name. weekly is then an empty list, the figures over three and five years and the correlated stocks are null or empty, calendar is given once 40 of the last 52 weeks have a return, and r1 once the weekly closes cover a full year. A security covered funds hold with no file of its own, a stock the price data does not list or lists too few weekly returns for, or a line listed abroad (7203.JP), answers with "coverage": "holders_only": its holders from the shard of its first character, each dated, the price and return fields null, and none of the fields built from each fund's file or the ledger, such as etf_ownership and holders_all. A 404 means no covered fund holds the key. Read coverage first: since October 2026, holders_only marks an answer without the fields Security requires and SecurityHoldersOnly does not list, such as etf_ownership, holders_all and answer.

example.ranking: By overlap, lowest first, then by weekly correlation, lowest first, each as printed (one and two decimals). An ETF with a figure not measured comes after those measured, then in the order asked. Two measurements, not a recommendation.

definitions.overlap: The sum, over the companies both hold, of the smaller of two weights: the company's weight in the candidate, and its weight in the portfolio, which is its weight in each of the portfolio's ETFs times that ETF's weight. An ETF that holds no shares adds nothing to the portfolio's side. For an ETF read from its SEC filings, a holding the filing lists on a market abroad matches only the same holding abroad.
definitions.share_of_candidate: The part of the candidate's weight in companies the portfolio also holds, each counted at the candidate's own weight. It is never below the overlap, which counts the smaller of the two weights.
definitions.correlation: Pearson's correlation between the candidate's weekly returns and the portfolio's, on the weeks both have: at most the 156 the files carry, at least 52. The portfolio's weekly return is the return of its ETFs at their weights, counting every ETF with at least 52 weekly returns here, whatever it holds. A weekly return is a weekly total return, from the last close of one week to the last close of the next, with dividends reinvested, as in the fund files. The weeks end on Fridays, or on the Thursday when the exchange is shut that Friday, and the last one ends on the files' last close.
definitions.down_weeks: The same correlation on the weeks the portfolio's return was below zero, when there are at least 20.

mega_cap_tech.rule: A fixed list, the one every fund file's breakdown and every ETF page count: Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Broadcom and Tesla, every listed class of each.

definitions.sectors: Each ETF's breakdown, as its fund file and ETF page give it. A company's sector is the one most of the single-sector index funds that hold it belong to, each fund one vote, or else the sector of its SEC industry code. When a sector is found for under 50% of an ETF's stock weight, no sector weight is given. A portfolio's breakdown is its ETFs' at their weights.
definitions.countries: Each ETF's breakdown, as its fund file gives it. A line listed abroad counts under the country of its market. A US-listed line counts under the United States, unless its company files with the SEC as a foreign issuer or is Canadian: it then counts under the country of the company's business address. A fund held by a fund counts under the United States.

One exception: the count of shares outstanding is used when it is at most 2% below a current independent count, so a figure can be up to about 2% of itself too high. definitions.shares_held: The sum, over the covered funds counted, of the shares each holds of every listed class of the company, each class counted at its weight. An issuer file gives the count of its row; a fund from SEC filings the share balance of its common stock rows in its latest Form N-PORT filing. A Vanguard ETF's file counts the whole fund, so its count is multiplied by the ETF class's net assets over the whole fund's, as Vanguard prints them, the first taken at the low end of its rounding and the second at the high end.
definitions.shares_outstanding: The count of the company's shares outstanding on the cover of a periodic report (a 10-K, 10-Q, 20-F or 40-F, amendments and transition reports included), tagged dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding in the SEC's XBRL data: the most recent one read, published with the date the cover counts the shares on and the filing it comes from. One figure, or one per class rolled up to the company, each class at its weight (one unless the charter says otherwise: a Berkshire class A share is 1,500 class B shares). A count the cover gives for another security, such as preferred stock, warrants, notes, the units of a partnership beside a class of shares or a fully diluted total, is no class and is left out. When the roll-up does not check out and the stock's own class does, the figure is the class's own count, and basis says so; one count read from a filing that names no other class of stock is the company's.
definitions.lower_bound: Funds not covered are not counted, nor covered funds whose count cannot be used, and the percent is rounded down. Holdings and the count carry their own dates, which differ; both are published with the figure. The count is used only when it is at most 2% below a current independent count of the same shares, so the count can put a figure at most about 2% of itself above what the current count would give.

rules: A fund is counted once. A fund in both layers is counted from its issuer file. A fund that holds another covered fund is read from its own book, so the shares it holds through that fund are counted there, once.

Only the rows under the stock's own ticker are counted, each the US line: a line listed abroad has a key of its own, its code and its market (7203.JP beside TM, Toyota's ADR), and is another security, never counted for a US stock. A Toronto line of a company whose shares trade in New York is the same shares, of the same class, and is counted under the US ticker (RY).

A row that is another security under the stock's ticker is not counted: the rows of a preferred stock fund, a row whose name in the issuer's file is a preferred or depositary share of the company, and a row whose value per share is more than 25% above or 20% below the stock's close on the row's date.

not_counted.no_share_count: its file gives no share count for the row
not_counted.through_fund: it holds the stock through another covered fund, which is counted instead
not_counted.preferred_fund: a preferred stock fund, whose row is a preferred share
not_counted.preferred_row: the row's name in the issuer's file is a preferred or depositary share of the company, filed under the common's ticker
not_counted.price_mismatch: the row's value per share is more than 25% above or 20% below the stock's close on its date, so the row is another security or a count in other shares
not_counted.value_mismatch: the file does not match its weights times the fund's stated net assets, so its counts are wrong or in other shares: for a file without market values, the row's count at the stock's close by more than 25% above or 20% below, or the fund's rows by more than 10% either way in their median; for a file with them, the fund's rows' values by more than 10% either way in their median
not_counted.no_value_check: the file gives no market values and the fund states no net assets, so its share count cannot be checked
not_counted.no_class_size: a Vanguard file without the ETF class's share of the fund
not_counted.whole_series: an SEC filing that covers mutual fund classes too
not_counted.before_split: the row is dated before a split of the stock, so its count is in the old shares
not_counted.before_first_close: the row is dated before the stock's first close in the price data, so it is not counted against this listing
not_counted.single_issuer_file: the only issuer file counted, whose count is never published alone

refusals.no_sec_count: the SEC data gives no count of the company's shares
refusals.class_unknown: the company's filing does not say which class this ticker is
refusals.count_too_old: the company's count is more than 400 days older than the holdings
refusals.count_date_invalid: the company's count is dated after the newest holdings, a slip in the filing's data
refusals.no_independent_count: no independent count to check the SEC's count against
refusals.split_between_dates: a split of the stock falls after the date of the SEC's count, which is in the old shares
refusals.count_below_independent: the SEC's count is more than 2% below a current independent count of the same shares, so the percent would be too high
refusals.count_mismatch: the SEC's count is far above an independent count of the same shares, so it counts other shares
refusals.no_fund_counted: no covered fund's share count could be used
refusals.under_0_01_pct: the counted funds hold less than 0.01% of the shares, below the two decimals of the figure
refusals.above_100: the count comes to more than 100% of the shares
refusals.held_back: tonight's ledger failed its checks, and the last one that passed, served in its place, has no line for this stock, or there is none

methods.name: ETF Ownership Index
methods.measures: For each US company, the share of its shares outstanding held by the covered US ETFs (the ledger's figure, a lower bound), how concentrated that ownership is in the three funds holding the most, and how it changed over the last 5 and 20 market closes in the funds read daily from their issuers' files; and the same over the market and by sector, weighted by market cap.
methods.formula: pct = ledger pct_lower_bound; top3_share = round(100 * sum of the 3 largest fund holdings / shares_held, 1 decimal); change_nd_pp = round(100 * sum over the last n closes of net_shares / shares_outstanding, 4 decimals); cap_weighted_pct = floor(sum(pct * cap) / sum(cap), 2 decimals)

definitions.pct: The figure of the ETF ownership ledger (ti-ownership/1): at least this percent of the company's shares outstanding, from the SEC's count, is held by the covered US ETFs. Its rules, refusals and test vectors are those of that method.
definitions.top3_share: The shares held by the three counted funds holding the most, over the shares held by every counted fund, in percent. A fund holding two classes of the company is one fund, each class at its weight. Published when at least 6 funds are counted and no sum the stock file publishes gives back one fund's count by difference with it.
definitions.net_shares: What the funds read daily from their issuers' files bought less what they sold of the stock on one market close, as the ETF flows (ti-flows/1) publish it: a sum over three funds or more, no fund more than 80% of it, the lines a split, a merger or a spin-off moved left out.
definitions.change_nd_pp: The sum of net_shares over the last n market closes, every listed class at its weight on a company basis, over the ledger's count of shares outstanding, in percentage points. The funds known from SEC filings are not in it.
definitions.cap_weighted_pct: Over one company line per company on a company basis: the sum of pct times market cap over the sum of market caps, a lower bound of the share of those companies' combined market value held by the covered US ETFs.

rules: A figure of one class alone (basis class) is in the stock rows and left out of the market and sector lines, since a class's percent is not the company's.
A company with several listed classes is one line, under the ticker with the largest market cap.

top3_share is null under 6 funds counted. The stock file publishes the shares held by layer and by class, and the counts of the funds known from SEC filings are on EDGAR, so the funds read from issuer files among the three largest, and those beside them, fall into groups whose sums can be had by difference: each layer's, and each class's whose shares held are published, the other classes together. Each group must be empty or a sum over 3 funds or more, no fund above 80% of it, or top3_share is null.

A change is null when a daily sum of its window is withheld, when the flows name a corporate action of the stock within the window or 3 closes before it, when a close of the window is not a complete close of the flows, and when no fund read daily held or moved the stock in the flows' window.
A line's change is the cap-weighted mean of the changes of its companies that have one, with the share of the line's cap they make up.
A sector has a line when it has at least 5 companies. The sector is the price data's, which covers the companies of its S&P 500 list.

The daily history keeps one line per market close, written on the first night that close is published and never rewritten. The closes before the first night are rebuilt from the flows of that night: their changes only.

not_counted.window_not_covered: A close of the window is not a complete close of the flows, or the window starts before the first close they publish.
not_counted.withheld: A daily sum of the window is withheld by the flows' rules, so the change would give it back.
not_counted.corporate_action: The flows name a corporate action of the stock within the window or just before it.
not_counted.not_in_flows: No fund read daily from its issuer's files held or moved the stock in the flows' window.

refusals.fewer_than_6_funds: Fewer than 6 funds are counted, so the three largest or the rest would be a sum over fewer than three funds.
refusals.split_under_3_funds: With the shares held by layer or by class that the stock file publishes, the share of the three largest would leave one or two funds read from issuer files in a group whose sum can be had by difference.
refusals.one_fund_dominant: With the shares held by layer or by class that the stock file publishes, the share of the three largest would leave a group of funds read from issuer files in which one fund holds more than 80%.
refusals.not_in_ledger: The ledger served tonight was made before the concentration was measured.

methods.measures: How much two funds hold of the same securities, by weight: one figure that is the same from either side, and the share of each fund's own weight that sits in the securities both hold.

definitions.shared keys: The keys both maps hold, compared exactly as written.
definitions.n_shared: How many keys both maps hold.

share_of_a is over the first fund's listed total weight, which can differ a little from 100; by_weight is not rescaled.
A figure is rounded once, at the end, to one decimal.

expense_ratio.description: Annual cost as a percentage of assets: 0.03 means three basis points, or $3 a year on $10,000. From the fund's newest SEC filing that states it, after any fee waiver when the filing gives both figures, else from the market data. Null when neither gives one. Never read a null as zero.

expense_ratio_gross.description: The total of the filing's fee table before any waiver, in percent, which counts the fees of the funds it holds; expense_ratio when there is no waiver. Null unless expense_ratio is from a filing.

expense_ratio_source.description: Where expense_ratio comes from. sec_filing: the fee table the filing tags by share class, from the SEC's risk/return data sets or the filing itself. sec_filing_text: the fee table's text, read in a newer prospectus, where no other figure exists or one agrees with it. market_data: undated, also where the filing read is over a year old and differs, or is not matched to the fund. Null when expense_ratio is null.

expense_ratio_as_of.description: The day that filing reached the SEC, or null.

expense_ratio_filing_url.description: That filing on EDGAR, or null.

yield.description: Trailing twelve month distribution yield, as a percentage.

aum_b.description: Assets under management, in billions of US dollars, rounded to 0.1, from the market data, read on aum_date. For a Vanguard fund it is the whole fund, every share class together; etf_class_net_assets_b is the ETF's own class. Null when the market data gives no size, the usual case for an SEC-layer fund, whose size is then net_assets on report_date.

aum_source.description: Where aum_b comes from. market_data: read on aum_date. market_data_kept: the latest read gave no size, so the last size known is kept, with the day it was read, for 30 days at most. Null when aum_b is null.

aum_date.description: The day aum_b was read from the market data. Null when aum_b is null, or for a size read before the day was recorded.

etf_class_net_assets_b.description: For a Vanguard fund, the net assets of its ETF share class alone, in billions of US dollars, as Vanguard states them. Such a fund's ETF is one class of a fund that also has mutual fund classes. Every value held in /api/v1/sec/{ticker}.json is computed from it for such a fund. Null for any other fund.

etf_class_net_assets_as_of.description: The date Vanguard gives for etf_class_net_assets_b. Null when it is.

derivative_positions.description: The derivative positions the filing lists, before the legs roll them up.

vol.description: Annualised standard deviation of weekly total returns over three years, as a percentage.

beta.description: Sensitivity to the S&P 500, from three years of weekly returns. 1.00 means it has moved with the index.

mdd3.description: Largest peak to trough decline over three years, measured on weekly closes. Negative.

r1.description: Cumulative total return over one year, as a percentage. Not annualised.

r3.description: Cumulative total return over three years, as a percentage. Not annualised.

r5.description: Cumulative total return over five years, as a percentage. Not annualised.

last_close.description: The last closing price, raw, in the fund's trading currency. Returns use dividend-adjusted closes; this figure is the market close as traded.

day_change_pct.description: The move from the previous close to the last, as a percentage.

high_52w.description: The highest raw close over the last 252 trading days.

low_52w.description: The lowest raw close over the last 252 trading days.

currency.description: The trading currency of the price fields.

held_outright.description: What the fund holds outright: a map of ticker to percent of net assets, never its contracts (see derivatives).

summary.description: One sentence to quote: what the fund held, and for a trust the filing that says so.

composition.description: What the fund holds, as [{kind, label, pct}] in percent of net assets, largest first. kind is what the filing classes each line as: stocks, treasury_bills, treasury_notes_and_bonds, agency_debt, agency_mortgage_pools, corporate_bonds, municipal_bonds, money_market_funds, repurchase_agreements and the like. A trust lists its asset, pct 100.0 when it is the only investment and null where the filing gives no split.

derivatives.description: Swaps, futures and options, one leg per instrument, underlying and direction: instrument, description, underlying or underlying_ticker, underlying_kind, direction (the fund's side; a written option is short), notional_pct (the size the filing states, in percent of net assets; null when it gives none in dollars, always for a pool; an option's is strike times shares), value_pct, positions, option_type, option_side, expires_first, expires_last.

underlyings.description: The legs rolled up by underlying: long_pct and short_pct of swaps and futures, options by kind and side, instruments, net_pct, complete.

exposure.description: stocks_pct; swaps_futures_long_pct and swaps_futures_short_pct; options_notional_pct; complete; long_exposure_pct, stocks plus long swaps and futures when the fund has no short leg or option and every size is stated (TQQQ: about 300), else null.

exposure_notes.description: Caveats about the sizes, in words.

weekly.description: 156 weekly total returns as decimals, oldest first, ending at as_of. The weeks are the same in every fund and stock file, so any basket of them can be correlated without matching dates. A week is null when its return cannot be computed, because the fund's prices begin later or a weekly close is missing. An empty list for an issuer-layer fund with fewer than 110 weekly returns in those weeks, and null for a fund of another layer with fewer.

weeks_end.description: The date the weekly series ends, always as_of. It is set even when weekly is an empty list, and null, like as_of, when weekly is null.

license.description: The licence the data is published under.

attribution.description: How to credit the data: a link to the page cite_as names where the medium allows one, the name where it does not.

source.description: Where the method behind these figures is written down.

structure.description: The kind of trust or pool.

source_form.description: The SEC form the description was checked against.

target.description: The daily multiple a geared pool seeks (2x, -2x); null otherwise.

filing_lines.description: The lines the filing has, for a fixed income or multi-asset fund: a count, not holdings.

fixed_income.description: A fixed income fund's figures, over every line of its filing: average_coupon_pct, average_maturity_years (a mortgage pool counts at its final maturity), duration_years (from the fund's own interest rate risk figures, null when it gives none), debt_pct, by_maturity, by_country and issuers [{issuer, key, pct, lines}], largest first, with issuers_total and issuers_shown_pct. Issuer overlap: the sum over shared key of the smaller pct.

lines.description: The largest lines of the filing by name, with no identifier: issuer, kind, coupon_pct, maturity (a date, or the year of a group of mortgage pools), pct, count of filing lines it stands for and, for an ETF this API covers, ticker.

notes.description: Caveats about the lines, in words. In a sponsor file, also how its weights are read (swap and futures weights are the sponsor's own, as notional in percent of net assets).

sponsor.description: The sponsor whose site was read; in a prospectus file, its adviser.

file_date.description: The date of the sponsor's file.

served_from_earlier_file.description: True when an earlier night's file is kept.

lines_total.description: Lines not keyed and not a contract.

objective_cut.description: True when cut, ending in three dots.

stated_target.description: The daily multiple and reference the prospectus states, or null.

index.description: The index it tracks, or null.

expense_ratio_pct.description: Expenses in percent, after a waiver; null if not read.

inception_date.description: The start date it states, or null.

holdings_note.description: Says its first holdings filing replaces this file.

page_url.description: The stock's page on the site, or null when it has none. Link this when quoting the figures.

cite_as.description: A citation line for a quoted figure: company, sources and date, a URL to check it, licence.

cite_html.description: The credit as HTML: a link to the page cite_as names, then its address.

sector.description: The company's sector where the data classifies it, or "US Listed" when it does not, which is the case for most stocks.

industry.description: The finest level of that classification under the sector, such as Semiconductors or Regional Banks; null when sector is "US Listed".

asset_type.description: etf for a fund; etn for an exchange-traded note, a bank's debt with no holdings; stock for any other listed share: a company's stock, a depositary receipt, a closed-end fund.

exchange.description: The exchange the security is listed on, as Nasdaq Trader's directory names it: Nasdaq, NYSE, NYSE Arca, Cboe BZX and the others its codes stand for. Null when the directory does not list it. Unlike the identifiers, it changes when the listing moves.

composite_figi.description: The Financial Instrument Global Identifier of the US listing (the composite FIGI of exchange code US), from OpenFIGI, asked by ticker. FIGIs are in the public domain. Null until OpenFIGI answers for the ticker with one security of this asset type.

share_class_figi.description: The FIGI of the share class, the same on every market it trades in. Null with composite_figi.

cik.description: The SEC's Central Index Key, ten digits as EDGAR writes it, from the SEC's ticker files: the company's, or for a fund the registrant's, the trust that files for it and for its other funds. Several securities can share one, so key records on composite_figi or class_id instead. Null when the SEC's files do not list the ticker.

series_id.description: For a fund, the SEC's id of its series (S and nine digits), which tells it apart from the other funds of its registrant: from the SEC's fund ticker file, or from the Form N-PORT its holdings are read from where the two differ. Null for a stock, and for a trust that files as a company.

class_id.description: For a fund, the SEC's id of its share class (C and nine digits). Null when series_id is, or when it comes from the Form N-PORT and the fund ticker file lists the ticker under another series.

as_of.description: The price date: the date of the price data behind every figure here.

page.description: True when the stock has a written page at /stock/{ticker}/. Every stock here has this file whether or not it has a page.

cap_b.description: Market capitalisation, in billions of US dollars.

yield.description: Trailing twelve month dividend yield, as a percentage.

vol.description: Annualised standard deviation of weekly total returns over three years, as a percentage.

beta.description: Sensitivity to the S&P 500, from three years of weekly returns.

mdd3.description: Largest peak to trough decline over three years, measured on weekly closes. Negative.

r1.description: Cumulative total return over one year, as a percentage. Not annualised.

r3.description: Cumulative total return over three years, as a percentage. Not annualised.

r5.description: Cumulative total return over five years, as a percentage. Not annualised.

last_close.description: The last closing price, raw, in the trading currency. Returns use dividend-adjusted closes; this is the close as traded.

day_change_pct.description: The move from the previous close to the last, as a percentage.

high_52w.description: The highest raw close over the last 252 trading days, or since the listing for a stock listed less than a year ago.

low_52w.description: The lowest raw close over the last 252 trading days, or since the listing for a stock listed less than a year ago.

currency.description: The trading currency of the price fields.

calendar.description: Total return by calendar year, as a percentage, the current year to date.

held_by.description: How many issuer-layer funds hold it, the rows of holders. The stock's page counts these less left_out, with the SEC-layer funds of held_by_sec_nport, as holders_all lists them.

heaviest.description: The issuer-layer fund that gives it the largest weight, as [fund ticker, weight percent]. Null when none of them holds it.

held_by_sec_nport.description: How many SEC-layer funds hold it, the rows of holders_sec_nport. The stock's page counts them with the issuer-layer funds and lists them in a table of their own, each linked to its filing.

holders.description: Every issuer-layer fund that holds it, heaviest first, as [fund ticker, weight percent, date of that fund's holdings file]. The same rows as the holders index, in the stock's own file.

holders_sec_nport.description: The SEC-layer funds that hold it, heaviest first, as [fund ticker, weight percent, the quarter end the filing describes]. They are months older than holders, so they are kept apart. A fund whose row under this ticker is a foreign company's local code is not listed. A filing names a security by its ISIN, which does not say where the fund bought it. So shares that trade in New York and abroad on one ISIN (AstraZeneca, TotalEnergies, Ferrari) are listed here for the funds whose stocks are mostly on US ISINs, and under the line abroad (AZN.GB) for the others. A preferred share is keyed by its issuer's common ticker, as the filings key it, so a preferred stock fund can appear here. For a stock whose weekly is empty, a row can be dated before its first close in the price data. Such a row can be another security that had the ticker, or the company's shares abroad before it listed in New York, and etf_ownership does not count it (before_first_close).

synthetic_exposure.description: The derivative-based funds whose swaps, futures or options reference the stock, largest first: fund, exposure (long, short, long and short, options, not stated), long_pct, short_pct, options, instruments, complete, report_date. Notional exposure, not shares held: in no holder list, rank or etf_ownership.

left_out.description: An empty list for a stock with a page, and null without one; kept for compatibility. Before lines listed abroad were keyed with their market (7203.JP), it named the issuer-layer funds whose row under the ticker was most likely a company listed abroad under the same code. Today a row stays under a US ticker when its issuer's file places it in New York, by its exchange, its currency or its identifiers, with the US list for a line nothing else places. The Toronto line of the same shares as a New York line also stays under the US ticker (RY). A row in dollars that nothing places abroad counts as a US line, as a few depositary receipts traded in London do (SBID, the GDR of State Bank of India).

same_code_abroad.description: The lines listed outside the United States under the same local code, as [key, company name], most widely held first. Each is another security, and often another company: SAN.ES is Banco Santander in Madrid and SAN.FR Sanofi in Paris, beside SAN, the Santander ADR. Their issuer-layer holders are under those keys in the holders index. Their SEC-layer holders are in holders_sec_nport of the shard of their first character (/api/v1/holders/a.json for AZN.GB). An empty list when there is none.

earlier_key_reads_as.description: The keys this ticker reads as now, this ticker among them, when it was also the key of other lines before lines listed abroad were keyed with their market. CCO, Clear Channel Outdoor, was also Cameco's Toronto code, so it reads as CCO and CCJ; SAN reads as SAN, SAN.ES and SAN.FR. The same list as the aliases of the holders index. Null when the ticker was only ever this line.

pct_lower_bound.description: At least this percent of the shares outstanding is held by the covered US ETFs counted, rounded down to two decimals. It is of the company, every class counted, when basis is company, and of this ticker's class alone when basis is class. It is a lower bound: funds not covered, and covered funds whose count could not be used, are not in it. One exception: the count of shares outstanding is used when it is at most 2% below a current independent count, so the figure can be up to about 2% of itself too high. Null when no figure is published; refused says why.

basis.description: What the percent is of. company: all the company's shares outstanding, every class rolled up. class: this ticker's class alone, which is not the company's figure. It is company when shares_outstanding covers every class, rolled up (Alphabet's three classes; Berkshire's class A counted as 1,500 class B shares). It is also company when that count is the one count the company's cover gives and the company has one class of stock. It is class when the roll-up over the cover's classes does not check out against an independent count while this class's count does. It is also class when the one count the SEC gives is short of an independent company count and cannot be shown to be the company's. That happens when the filing names another class of stock (Mobileye's class B, Plains GP's class B shares), or when the count is a frames row. Null when no figure is published.

company.description: The company the figure is about, as cite_as names it. It is the stock's name without what names the listing rather than the company. That is its class (Alphabet Inc., not Alphabet Inc. (Class A)), a depositary receipt, a registry share or a closed-end fund (Ares Capital Corporation, not Ares Capital Corporation - Closed End Fund). It keeps a leading "The" when the company's name has one (The Walt Disney Company). On a company basis the figure covers every class; on a class basis cite_as names the class by its ticker (the outstanding shares of the PAGP class). Null when no figure is published.

shares_held.description: The shares the counted funds hold, in shares of this ticker's class, of every listed class on a company basis. Issuer files enter it only as a sum over at least two of them, never a single issuer file's count. SEC filings are public one by one, so a figure can rest on a single filing.

shares_held_by_layer.description: shares_held split between the issuers' own files (issuer_files) and SEC Form N-PORT filings (sec_nport).

shares_outstanding.description: The company's shares outstanding, in shares of this ticker's class, as the cover of a periodic report states them in the SEC's XBRL data: a 10-K, 10-Q, 20-F or 40-F, amendments and transition reports included. It is the most recent count read; its date is shares_outstanding_as_of and its filing shares_outstanding_filing. On a class basis, it is the class's own count.

shares_outstanding_as_of.description: The date the cover counts the shares on. It is not the date of the holdings, which holdings_dates gives.

shares_outstanding_filing.description: The filing on SEC EDGAR the count comes from, to check it against the source.

funds_holding.description: How many covered funds list the stock, any listed class on a company basis, by layer: issuer_files and sec_nport. A fund holding two classes is one fund.

funds_counted.description: How many of them are counted in shares_held, by layer. The others are in not_counted.

funds_prorated.description: How many of the counted funds are Vanguard ETFs. A Vanguard file lists the whole fund, every share class together, so each is counted for its ETF class only. Its shares are multiplied by the ETF class's net assets over the whole fund's, as Vanguard prints them, each taken at the end of its rounding that keeps the figure a lower bound.

not_counted.description: The funds listing the stock that are not counted, by reason; each reason is explained under not_counted in /api/v1/methods.json. no_share_count: the file gives no share count. through_fund: held through another covered fund. preferred_fund: a preferred stock fund. preferred_row: a row the file names as a preferred or depositary share. price_mismatch: a value per share that is not the stock's price. value_mismatch: a file whose counts or values do not match its weights times the fund's stated net assets. no_value_check: a file without market values, and no net assets to check it against. no_class_size: a Vanguard file without its class sizes. whole_series: a filing covering mutual fund classes. before_split: a row dated before a split of the stock. before_first_close: a row dated before the stock's first close in the price data. single_issuer_file: the only issuer file counted. A fund holding two classes of the company is one fund here, and it is not listed when either of its rows is counted; rows_not_counted has the rows.

rows_not_counted.description: The rows not counted, one per fund and class, by the same reasons. It holds the row of a fund counted through another class that is itself left out, such as a preferred depositary share filed under the common's ticker. On a class basis, only this ticker's rows.

holdings_dates.description: The oldest and newest holdings dates of the counted funds. A filing describes a quarter end months back, so the two are often far apart.

holdings_dates_by_layer.description: The same for each layer, issuer_files and sec_nport; null for a layer with no fund counted.

weight.description: What one share of this class counts for, in shares of the ticker's class, when that is not one share (Berkshire's class A, 1,500 class B shares). Absent otherwise.

classes.description: For a company with several classes of stock, one entry per class: class, tickers (empty for an unlisted class), shares_outstanding and as_of. weight is set where one share counts for more than one share of this ticker's class. shares_held and pct_lower_bound are set where the class's own count checks out against its ticker's and the class figure is at least 0.01%, and are null otherwise. Null for a company with one class.

refused.description: Why no figure is published, as a code: no_sec_count, class_unknown, count_too_old, count_date_invalid, no_independent_count, split_between_dates, count_below_independent, count_mismatch, no_fund_counted, under_0_01_pct, above_100 or held_back. Null when a figure is published.

failures.description: How many stocks came to over 100% tonight.

figures.description: How many figures tonight's ledger has.

last_figures.description: How many the ledger served has.

last_as_of.description: The as_of of the ledger served.

held_back.description: Null on a normal night. When tonight's ledger failed its checks and was held back, the same object as held_back in /api/v1/ownership.json, and the figure here, if any, is from the last ledger that passed, with its own dates.

method.description: The method and its version, ti-ownership/1. A change to what it computes from inputs it already accepted is a new version.

method_url.description: Where the method is written down, with its test vectors.

cite_as.description: A citation line for the figure: company, the figure, the method, the holdings dates and the date of the count, a URL to check it, licence. Null when no figure is published.

cite_html.description: The credit as HTML: a link to the page cite_as names, then its address. Null when no figure is published.

etf_ownership.description: The stock's line of the ETF ownership ledger: the share of the company's shares outstanding that the covered US ETFs hold, at least, with its parts and dates, or why no figure is published. Its fields are described below; the method, with its test vectors, is /api/v1/methods.json.

holders_all.description: Every covered fund holding the stock, both layers in one list, heaviest first, an issuer file first on a tie. Each row is [fund ticker, weight percent, date of its holdings, layer, rank of the stock in the fund, the fund's positions, value held in millions of US dollars]. The layer is issuer for an issuer's own file, or sec_nport for an SEC Form N-PORT filing, dated to the quarter end it describes. The rank is 1 plus the number of the fund's positions that weigh more. The value held is the weight times the fund's net assets as published. Those are the ETF share class's for a Vanguard fund (etf_class_net_assets_b), aum_b for another issuer-layer fund, and net_assets for an SEC-layer fund. A value keeps the significant figures of the less precise of the weight and the net assets, three at most. VOO's value is 81000 on net assets Vanguard prints as $1.0 trillion, two figures; a fund with aum_b of 41.8 gives three. The value is null when the fund has no net assets, or has them to fewer than two figures, or when its filing covers mutual fund classes too. Fewer than two figures means aum_b under 1.0, which the market data gives to $0.1 billion, so 0.1 is anything from 0.05 to 0.15. rank_summary counts these funds in funds_without_value. The rows are the funds of holders, less left_out, and of holders_sec_nport; no fund is in both layers. A short position, a negative weight in a long and short fund, is listed with its negative weight and value. It is not a holding: rank_summary counts it in short_positions, and by_issuer, top_by_value, membership and answer leave it out.

funds.description: How many covered funds hold the stock: the rows of holders_all less short_positions.

top_holding_in.description: How many of them have it as their largest holding, a tie included.

top10_in.description: How many have it among their ten largest holdings.

funds_without_value.description: How many of them have no value held: no net assets, net assets known to fewer than two figures, or a filing that covers mutual fund classes too.

short_positions.description: How many funds hold the stock short, a negative weight in holders_all: listed there, never counted as holders.

funds.description: How many covered funds hold the stock: the rows of holders_all less short_positions.

top_holding_in.description: How many of them have it as their largest holding, a tie included.

top10_in.description: How many have it among their ten largest holdings.

funds.description: How many covered funds hold the stock: the rows of holders_all less short_positions.

top_holding_in.description: How many of them have it as their largest holding, a tie included.

top10_in.description: How many have it among their ten largest holdings.

funds.description: How many covered funds hold the stock: the rows of holders_all less short_positions.

top_holding_in.description: How many of them have it as their largest holding, a tie included.

top10_in.description: How many have it among their ten largest holdings.

by_layer.description: The same three counts for each layer, issuer and sec_nport.

rank_summary.description: How many of the holders have the stock as their largest holding (top_holding_in) and among their ten largest (top10_in), of how many (funds), in all and by layer. It also counts the holders with no value held (funds_without_value) and the funds short the stock (short_positions), which are not counted as holders.

value_usd_m.description: The value of the stock the fund holds, in millions of US dollars: weight times net_assets_b, to the significant figures of the less precise of the two, three at most.

weight.description: The stock's weight in the fund, in percent.

holdings_as_of.description: The date of the fund's holdings.

net_assets_b.description: The net assets the value is computed from, in billions of US dollars.

net_assets_basis.description: What they are: etf_class, a Vanguard ETF share class alone; fund, aum_b from the market data; filing, the net assets the fund's SEC filing states.

net_assets_as_of.description: Their date: Vanguard's, the day aum_b was read, or the filing's quarter end. Null when not known.

top_by_value.description: The ten holders with the most dollars in the stock, most first, each with the net assets its value is computed from and their date. Only funds with a value are ranked, so a fund whose net assets are known to fewer than two figures is not.

kind.description: broad for VOO, SPY, IVV, QQQ, VTI and SCHD, sector for a sector or industry fund.

category.description: The fund's category label, or null.

held.description: Whether the fund holds the stock.

weight.description: Its weight in percent, or null.

rank_in_fund.description: Its rank in the fund, 1 for the largest holding, or null.

positions.description: How many positions the fund holds.

holdings_as_of.description: The date of the fund's holdings.

membership.description: Whether the stock is in VOO, SPY, IVV, QQQ, VTI and SCHD, and in the three largest sector or industry funds holding it. Each comes with its weight, the stock's rank in it, its positions and the date of its holdings. The sector funds are ranked by the net assets a value is computed from. A fund is a sector fund when its TickerInside category is in the sector group (/etf/category/), else when its name names a sector or an industry. A fund no layer covers is left out.

issuer.description: The issuer, as the issuer files name it (iShares, SPDR, Vanguard, Invesco, Global X) or as a fund's name or filer gives it.

funds.description: How many of its covered funds hold the stock.

value_usd_m.description: The value they hold, in millions of US dollars, over the funds with a value, to the precision of the least precise of them; null when none has one.

funds_without_value.description: How many of them have no value, for want of published net assets known to two figures or more.

heaviest.description: The fund that gives the stock its largest weight, as [fund, weight percent].

largest.description: The fund holding the most dollars of it, as [fund, millions of US dollars], or null.

by_issuer.description: The six issuers whose covered funds hold the most dollars of the stock, most first. For each: how many of its funds hold it, the dollars in millions over the funds with a value, how many have none, the heaviest weight as [fund, weight percent] and the largest holding as [fund, millions of US dollars]. An issuer file names its issuer. An SEC-layer fund takes the issuer its name and the trust that filed it give, and one with none is left out.

fee_usd_per_1000.description: US dollars a year of the fund's expense ratio for each $1,000 of the stock held through it.

expense_ratio.description: The fund's expense ratio, in percent a year.

weight.description: The stock's weight in the fund, in percent.

holdings_as_of.description: The date of the fund's holdings.

fee_per_1000.description: The five cheapest ways to hold the stock through a covered fund: what the fund's expense ratio costs a year for each $1,000 of the stock held through it. It is 1000 times the expense ratio over the weight, both in percent. Only funds whose expense ratio is in the data are listed.

name.description: The company's name as compared: its trade name less the words a filed name ends in (SoFi, not SoFi Technologies).

count.description: How many covered funds' names contain it.

It gives the name compared, how many funds, and up to ten of them, holders first, each with whether it holds the stock. Null when there is none, or when the name is one word found in the funds of three issuers or more: a word of fund names more than a company's.

answer.description: One sentence to quote, built from the fields above and etf_ownership, every figure with its date. It says how many covered funds hold the stock, by layer, and how many have it as their largest holding. It says where it weighs most (under 0.01% for a weight that rounds to nothing) and where the most dollars are, with about as many figures as the value has (under $0.1 million below that). It ends with the ownership figure when there is one: every class counted when it counts several, also when no fund holds this class. It opens on the name the stock's page uses, or for a stock without a page on the company's name as etf_ownership.company gives it, with the class when the figure counts several. It calls the funds the ownership figure counts "N of them" when they are among the holders it has just counted and the figure counts one class.

least_correlated.description: The eight stocks least correlated with this one over the last 104 of the same weekly returns, as [ticker, correlation, name]. The candidates are stocks held by ten or more covered funds, so every neighbour is reachable through ETFs. A measurement of co-movement, not a recommendation.

most_correlated.description: The eight most correlated, same shape and same candidate set.

weekly.description: 156 weekly total returns as decimals, oldest first, ending at as_of: the same weeks as the fund files, so a stock and a fund correlate with the same arithmetic as two funds. A week is null when its return cannot be computed, because the stock's prices begin later or a weekly close is missing. At least 110 of the 156 are numbers. It is an empty list for a stock with fewer that has a file by the rule of this endpoint: its vol, beta, mdd3, r3 and r5 are then null and its correlated stocks empty lists.

weeks_end.description: The last date covered by the weekly series.

companies.description: The ten companies, one ticker each: the largest by the market data's capitalisation among the US companies any covered fund holds. A US company is a stock the price data places in a sector, or one whose company files 10-K and 10-Q reports with the SEC. A company with no stock file here is ranked like the others, and its weight in each fund counts in pct. A stock has a file with at least 110 of the 156 weekly returns, or with fewer when a fund read from an issuer file or a stock ETF from SEC filings holds it in a file dated since it listed, the price data has its closes since its listing, or a year of them, the last at most five sessions old, and Nasdaq Trader's directory lists it under its name.

funds_without_net_assets.description: How many US stock funds were left out because their files state no net assets.

net_assets_dates.description: The oldest and newest date of the net assets used: issuer figures are current, SEC filings months old.

top10_share.description: The share of the money in the covered US stock ETFs that sits in the ten largest US companies by market value. It gives pct, the companies, and funds, how many funds it is measured over: those whose net assets are at least 80% in US-listed stocks. It also gives how many such funds were left out for want of stated net assets, and the oldest and newest date of the net assets used. Each fund counts by its own net assets, a Vanguard fund by its ETF class's alone. The ten are ranked among every US company a covered fund holds, whether or not it has a stock file here. The weight of a company without a file counts as US stock like any other.

most_widely_held.description: The 25 companies held by the most covered funds, both layers, one line per company. Each line is [ticker, company name, how many covered funds hold any of its listed classes, the ticker's pct_lower_bound or null, its basis or null]. A fund holding two classes of the company (GOOGL and GOOG) is one fund. The ticker is the company's class held by the most funds. Its pct_lower_bound is that stock file's figure, of the company or of the ticker's class alone as basis says (Visa's is its class A's). A fund whose row under a ticker is another security is not counted: a preferred stock fund, a row named as a preferred share, or a filing whose row is listed under abroad. A line listed abroad has a key of its own (7203.JP beside TM) and is never counted for a US company.

failures.description: How many stocks came to over 100% tonight.

figures.description: How many figures tonight's ledger has.

last_figures.description: How many the ledger served has.

last_as_of.description: The as_of of the ledger served.

held_back.description: Null on a normal night. When tonight's ledger is held back, the figures served are those of the last ledger that passed, each with its own dates, and this says why. reason is above_100 when more than five stocks come to over 100% with no split to explain them; failures says how many, and examples which. It is fewer_figures when tonight's ledger has more than 20% fewer figures than the last one that passed (figures, last_figures), a night that lost an input. It is error when the ledger could not be computed tonight; top10_share is then null and most_widely_held empty. A fewer_figures hold lasts at most seven days of holdings dates (last_as_of is the date of the ledger served); after that the lower count is published. The ledger served keeps only the stocks that have a file tonight.

A US line is keyed by its ticker, and a dot and one letter mark a US share class (BRK.B). Any other line is keyed by its local code and its market, a dot and a two letter country code (7203.JP, SAN.FR). The Toronto line of a Canadian company that also trades in New York is the same shares, under the US ticker (RY). Preferred shares a file writes under their issuer's common ticker are under that ticker and .PFD, three letters and never a market (JPM.PFD). That key holds every series of JPMorgan's preferred stock a fund holds, and in a preferred stock fund any other income security filed under the ticker, such as a business development company's listed notes. It is a US line of its own, so a preferred stock fund is never listed among the holders of the common stock.

A key that became several was several companies or lines under one code. The shard of each old key's first character lists them all. This file leaves out a key that reads only as itself with its market after it (NESN as NESN.CH).

sec_nport.description: funds, how many other US stock ETFs are served from SEC filings; dataset, the SEC quarterly data set the layer was last read from (a fund with a newer filing on EDGAR is served from that filing); report_dates, the oldest and newest quarter end the filings describe.

universe.description: The coverage measured against the US-listed ETFs, the block of index.json coverage.universe.

archive.description: What the archive of issuer files holds: funds; snapshots, one per fund and file date; first and last, the oldest and newest file dates; and since, the day the archive began, which is not the oldest file date. ownership.description: The ETF ownership ledger: method; stocks, how many stocks have a figure; as_of, the newest holdings date it counted; held_back. held_back is true on a night whose ledger failed its checks, when the figures served are those of the last ledger that passed. data.description: The date of each layer of the data: prices, the issuers' files and the SEC filings, and of the ownership ledger computed from them.

published.description: How many pages the site publishes.

redated.description: How many of them this build dated as modified. Most nights it is a small number: a page is dated only when a reader would notice the change.

redated_paths.description: The first 50 of those pages, sorted.

pages.description: How many pages the site publishes, and which of them this build dated as modified in the sitemaps.

api.description: The API version, which is also the path prefix: v1.

mcp_package.description: The npm package tickerinside-mcp: name, version and its page.

mcp_remote.description: The remote MCP server: its URL and the version it announces.

live.description: The live checks of the site, made every five minutes: the file documented next.

method.description: How the checks are made, in one paragraph.

deployed.description: The version of the site serving now, or null before the first check saw it.

state.description: up or down for page, api and mcp; on time or late for the update; no data when no check has run for 15 minutes; unknown when the record could not be read.

since.description: When the current state began, within the last day, or null when it has held all day.

last_check.description: When the last check ran, in UTC.

last_ms.description: How long its answer took, in milliseconds, measured from the Cloudflare location that ran the check.

uptime_pct.description: The share of checks that passed over the last 24 hours, 7, 30 and 90 days. Slots with no check are left out.

no_data_pct_90d.description: The share of five-minute slots with no check over the period on record, up to 90 days.

open_incident.description: The id of the open incident on this check, or null.

ms_24h.description: The median and 95th percentile answer time over the last 24 hours, in milliseconds.

server_version.description: For the MCP server, the version its handshake announced.

last_build.description: For the update, the built_at of the last build seen.

prices_through.description: For the update, the price date of that build.

next_expected_by.description: For the update, the deadline of the next nightly build: 02:00 UTC the morning after a weekday.

components.description: One entry per check, with the fields of a component.

today.description: Today's figures so far, per check, in the shape of an entry of days.

days.description: Up to 90 days of daily figures, newest first: for each check, checks made, failed, no_data (slots with no check), up_pct and, except for the update, p50_ms and p95_ms. For the update, failed counts the checks that found it late.

incidents.description: Open incidents first, then those closed in the last 90 days: id, component, kind (down or late), started, ended, minutes and cause. An incident opens after two failed checks in a row and closes after two good ones.

status.description: The nightly report, as served at /api/v1/status.json.

license.description: The licence the data is published under.

error.description: Always not_covered, whatever the reason: read reason and the next address.

reason.description: Every code is explained on /contract/#reasons. not_in_directory: a fund address with no file, for a ticker not in the directory of US-listed funds; a ticker of the directory with no file gets the code universe.json gives it (etn, no_filing_yet and the others), and no_file when the directory was not read. not_held: under /sec/, no covered fund holds the key; earlier_key: an old key, with reads_as. no_such_endpoint: no endpoint at the address. funds_not_covered: several funds of /overlap or /lookthrough, with reasons. in_another_layer: sent only to the TickerInside clients released before /fund/ answered for a fund of the other layers too (see holdings_kind); etf gives the fund's file. has_security_file: a ticker asked for as a fund has a stock file (see security). is_a_fund: a ticker asked for as a stock is a covered fund (see fund, and holders for the funds that hold it). no_written_comparison: no comparison file for this pair in either order (see fund_files and written_comparisons). not_a_shard: an address under /api/v1/holders/ that is not a shard (see holders). Under /api/v1/history/: not_in_archive: the fund has no history file (see history). holdings_at_date_not_enabled: holdings at a date are not served yet, and every valid date answers this (see changes). invalid_date: the date is not a calendar date, or is after today. before_history: the date is before the fund's first file (see first), answered only once holdings at a date are served. Under /api/v1/flows/: reason not_held_by_daily_funds: no fund read daily from its issuer's files held the key or moved it in the last 20 trading days; summary names the night's summary.

ticker.description: What was asked for, upper case; null when the address names no single ticker, such as a pair under /compare/.

message.description: What happened and where to look next, in words.

security.description: With has_security_file: the stock file of the ticker, or its holders-only answer.

reads_as.description: Under /sec/, for an old key written before lines listed abroad carried their market (7203): the keys it reads as now, from the aliases of holders. Absent otherwise.

pair.description: With no_written_comparison: the two tickers asked for, upper case, or null when the address names no pair.

written_comparisons.description: With no_written_comparison: the pairs that have a comparison file, as index.json lists them.

fund_files.description: With no_written_comparison: the fund files of the tickers asked for that are covered funds, to compute the overlap from.

covered.description: What is covered: /api/v1/securities.json after a /sec/ address with no reason, /api/v1/index.json otherwise.

not_covered.description: Under /overlap, /lookthrough and /diversify: the tickers asked for that are not covered.

reasons.description: Under /overlap, /lookthrough and /diversify: the reason code of each ticker of not_covered.

covered_issuers.description: Under /overlap and /lookthrough: the issuers whose own files are read; the other covered funds are read from SEC filings.

history.description: With not_in_archive: the list of the funds that have a history.

changes.description: With holdings_at_date_not_enabled: the fund's changes file, served today.

first.description: With before_history: the date of the fund's oldest file. before_history is answered only once holdings at a date are served.

date.description: With invalid_date, holdings_at_date_not_enabled or before_history: the date asked for.

uptime.description: The live checks: whether the site fails its own checks.

as_of.description: The newest file date any fund's history reaches. Here as_of is a holdings file date, not the price date.

since.description: The oldest file date any fund's history starts from. It is not the day the archive began, which is since in status.json, under data.archive.

count.description: How many funds have a history file, the length of funds.

first.description: The date of the oldest file of the fund in the archive.

file_dates.description: How many file dates the archive holds for the fund.

cadence.description: daily when the median gap between two files is at most four days, monthly when it is 25 to 35 days, irregular otherwise; null with a single file.

traded_pp_from.description: The date of the first step whose two files both carry share counts, from which traded_pp is measured; null when there is none yet.

ended.description: Last issuer file's date once no longer read, else null.

funds.description: One entry per fund with a history, ended or not; its fields are described below.

holdings_at.description: The address of a fund's holdings at a date, with {ticker} and {date} to fill, once it is served; null until then. Today any valid date answers 404 not_covered, with reason holdings_at_date_not_enabled and the address of the fund's changes file.

key_scheme.description: The keys the holdings are given in: 2, the scheme of today's files, where a line listed abroad carries its market (7203.JP). Older files are read in these keys.

first.description: The date of the oldest file of the fund in the archive.

file_dates.description: How many file dates the archive holds for the fund.

cadence.description: daily, monthly or irregular, from the gaps between the file dates; null with a single file.

columns.description: The names of the columns of each row. holdings_as_of: the file date. positions: the lines in the file. top10_weight: the weight of its ten largest lines, in percent; null for the files of a fund of funds before its file kept the funds it holds apart from its own lines. key_scheme: the keys the file was written in, 1 or 2. Scheme 1 is for files read before the switch to keys with a market, late in September 2026. The switch date varies by fund (SPY's first scheme 2 file is dated 2026-09-25), and the first scheme 2 step is restated. unplaced: for a file of scheme 1, the old keys that cannot be read as one line today because they stood for two companies in that file (SAN for Santander and Sanofi); null for a file of scheme 2.

snapshots.description: One row per file date, oldest first, with the columns named in columns.

moved_threshold_pp.description: How far a weight has to move, in percentage points, for its line to be listed under moved: 0.05.

traded_min_pairs.description: How many steps with share counts on both sides a fund needs before traded_pp is published: 20.

traded_pairs.description: How many of the fund's steps have share counts on both sides.

traded_pp_from.description: The date of the first of those steps; null when there is none.

traded_pp_reason.description: Why traded_pp is null in every step: fewer_than_20_pairs_with_share_counts. Null once it is published.

changes.description: One entry per step from a file to the next, oldest first; its fields are described below.

with_top_funds_by_overlap.description: How many funds are followed: the funds whose overlap by weight with this one is highest on the latest files, up to ten.

series.description: For each followed fund, most overlapping first, [date, overlap by weight in percent] on every file date of either fund from the first date both have a file. Each fund is taken at its latest file on or before the date. It is the overlap by weight the comparisons print, computed here from the archived files. A file of the old key scheme is read in today's keys, so a point can differ from what a comparison printed on the day. A series can step where either fund's history is restated.

overlap_history.description: How the fund's overlap by weight with its ten closest funds moved; its fields are described below.

holdings_at.description: The address of the fund's holdings at any date, with {date} to fill, once it is served; null until then.

fund.description: The fund's current file, with its holdings today, cost, returns and risk.

ended.description: Null while read; once not, last_file, source_layer and note.

cite_as.description: A citation line: the fund, the dates of its oldest and newest files, and this file's address.

cite_html.description: The credit as HTML: a link to this file, then its address.

terms.description: The terms in full, on the legal notice.

attribution.description: How to credit it, a link to the file where the medium allows one and the name where it does not, then what the history terms allow.

date.description: The date of the file the step leads to.

previous.description: The date of the file it is compared with: the fund's file before it in the archive, days or a month earlier.

entered.description: The lines in this file that were not in the previous one, as [key, weight percent], heaviest first. Absent from a restated step, which does not say what entered or exited that day; the snapshots give only its count of positions. Read it with a default, such as step.get("entered", []). A key of digits and a letter is a code the issuer's file gives in place of a ticker. When a ticker exits and such a code enters at about the same weight, and the reverse follows, it is the same security re-keyed, not a trade.

exited.description: The lines in the previous file that are not in this one, as [key, weight percent in the previous file], heaviest first. Absent from a restated step.

moved.description: The lines in both files whose weight moved by moved_threshold_pp or more, as [key, weight before, weight after], largest move first. Absent from a restated step.

moved_below_threshold.description: How many other lines in both files moved by less. Absent from a restated step.

names_turnover_pp.description: Half the weight that entered plus the weight that exited, in percentage points: what the change of names carried. Null on a restated step.

weights_moved_pp.description: Half the sum of the absolute changes of weight over every line of either file, in percentage points. It includes price drift, which moves every weight a little each day, so it is not turnover. Null on a restated step.

traded_pp.description: What the share counts say was traded, in percentage points of assets, when both files carry them and the fund has traded_min_pairs such steps; null otherwise. A line held in both counts its weight times the change of its quantity beyond the fund's own growth, a line that entered or exited its weight, and the sum is halved.

splits_seen.description: The lines whose quantity moved by a split ratio while their weight did not, left out of traded_pp. Present when there is one.

reverted.description: The entered lines the fund held two files earlier, most often a line the issuer's file left out for a day. That exit and this entry are a glitch in the file, not trades, and so is a key of digits and a letter that stood in for the line in the file between. Present when there is one.

restated.description: true on a step that is a change of the keys or of the reading of the files, not a trade; absent otherwise. A restated step has no entered, exited, moved or moved_below_threshold, so read them with a default. It is set on the step to a file of the current key scheme, where the parser also reads lines the old one dropped. It is set on the first file of a fund of funds that lists the funds it holds apart from their look-through, and on two files whose weights add up to totals 50 points or more apart. It is also set on the first file that keys apart the preferred shares a file writes under their issuer's common ticker (JPM.PFD rather than JPM), and on a date listed after a fix of the reading.

reason.description: Why the step is restated. key_scheme_2: the first file in keys with a market. own_lines_separated: a fund of funds whose earlier files listed the funds it holds beside their look-through, about 200% in all. weight_total_changed: the two totals are 50 points or more apart. weights_from_market_values: weights from market values, or the reverse. preferred_keyed_apart: the preferred shares the file writes under their issuer's common ticker are keyed as that ticker and .PFD, at the weight the common ticker carried. Otherwise, the reason given with a listed date.

rekeyed.description: On a restated step, the old keys that read as other keys today, as [old key, [new keys]]. It covers a spelling brought together (A005930 is 005930.KR), a Toronto code under its New York ticker, and a key that stood for several lines, with the lines the new file holds. It also covers a common ticker whose preferred shares took a key of their own (JPM as [JPM.PFD], or [WFC, WFC.PFD] where the fund holds both).

market_added.description: On a restated step, how many old keys only took their market (7203 became 7203.JP). Each is in the aliases of the holders shard of its first character.

coverage_added_pp.description: On a restated step, the weight the new file covers beyond the previous one, in percentage points: lines the old reading dropped, or, below zero, weight the old reading counted twice.

kind.description: pair for two funds, matrix for three or more: which of the two shapes the answer has.

page_url.description: The web page whose HTML, as the server sends it, prints the answer's figure, so that it reads without JavaScript: for a pair, its written comparison when there is one, else its "Does it diversify me?" answer within that answer's limits; for three funds or more, the x-ray the site wrote of the same funds; for a look-through, the x-ray the site wrote of the portfolio at the same weights (listed under pages in /og/answers.json), or for one fund, its page. Null where no page prints the figure yet: any other overlap of three funds or more or look-through of two funds or more, a pair past those limits, a pair of bond funds.

share_url.description: The address whose HTML reproduces the whole answer on the site: for a pair, its "Does it diversify me?" answer within that answer's limits; for three funds or more and for a portfolio, the x-ray the site wrote of the same funds (listed under pages in /og/answers.json), each weight in percent to 0.01 point and never an amount, in the order of the funds the site wrote it in. Absent where no page prints the answer.

holdings_source.description: Each fund's source, by ticker: issuer file, SEC Form N-PORT, trust's own SEC filing, sponsor's own holdings file, or prospectus, no holdings yet.

overlap.description: For two funds holding shares, in percent: by_weight, the sum over the companies both hold of the smaller of their two weights; share_of_a and share_of_b, the part of each fund in companies the other holds too; companies_in_both, the holdings both have, counted by ticker (GOOGL and GOOG count as two), positions_a and positions_b; and largest_shared, the 15 largest shared holdings with each weight and the smaller one counted. A ticker the two hold for two different companies is left out of every figure and listed in same_ticker_two_companies, with same_ticker_note.

overlap_kind.description: issuer when the figures are an overlap by issuer, of fixed income funds. Absent otherwise.

issuer_overlap.description: For two fixed income funds: the overlap by issuer, the smaller weight of each issuer both hold summed (by_weight), the share of each, issuers_in_both, the issuers compared and the largest shared and unshared ones. Never mixed with the overlap by shares.

correlation_3y.description: The correlation of the two funds' weekly returns over up to three years, on the weeks both have. Null under 52 such weeks.

covariance_annualised_pct2.description: The annualised covariance of the same returns, in percent squared. Null with correlation_3y.

weeks_used.description: How many weeks the two figures above read. Null when they are.

funds.description: Each fund by ticker: name, expense_ratio_pct, return_3y_pct, volatility_pct, worst_fall_3y_pct, beta_vs_sp500 (three years, from its file), beta_vs_sp500_1y (the last 52 weeks against SPY's) and positions; a fixed income fund's average coupon, maturity and duration. Null where the data has no figure.

renamed.description: Each ticker asked that a fund had before it was renamed, with its ticker now, under which the answer reads and names it. Absent when there is none.

have.description: The portfolio of the funds held: each fund (funds) with its weight_pct, name, holdings_as_of, holdings_source, holds_shares and weekly_returns, the number of weekly returns its file has; weights, given or equal; looked_through_pct, the part of the portfolio in funds that hold shares; holds_no_shares; returns_from, the funds its weekly returns are computed from, and no_price_history; no_breakdown, the funds holding shares whose file gives no breakdown; mega_cap_tech_pct, sectors and countries as each candidate has them, its funds' at their weights, in percent of the whole portfolio; and its sentence.
