holdings_source.description: Its source: issuer file, SEC Form N-PORT, trust's own SEC filing, sponsor's own holdings file, or prospectus, no holdings yet.

fund_file.description: The address of its fund file.

overlap.description: In percent: by_weight_pct, the sum over the companies it and the portfolio both hold of the smaller of its weight and the portfolio's, the portfolio looked through its funds at their weights; share_of_candidate_pct, the part of the fund in those companies; companies_in_both, the holdings both have, counted by ticker; and largest_shared, up to five, each with in_candidate_pct, in_have_pct and counted_pct. correlation.description: Of weekly returns, the fund's against the portfolio's: weekly, over weeks weeks from from to to, each the last close of its week (weeks run Saturday to Friday: a week closes on its Friday, or on the Thursday when the exchange is shut that Friday, and the last week on the data's last close); down_weeks, the same on the down_weeks_count weeks the portfolio fell, null under 20 of them; and with, the funds held whose returns the portfolio's are computed from. volatility_pct.description: Its annualised weekly volatility over the weeks of its correlation, in percent; absent when the correlation is not measured.

with_10_pct.description: The portfolio's annualised weekly volatility with 10% in this ETF and 90% in the ETFs held at their weights, rebalanced weekly (volatility_pct), against the portfolio alone (instead_of_pct), over the weeks of its correlation; absent when the correlation is not measured.

sectors.description: From its fund file's breakdown: known_pct, the part of the fund whose sector is found; coverage_pct, that part of its stock weight; stated, whether coverage_pct reaches definitions.sectors_stated_from_pct; and weights, when stated, each sector with its id (sector), name and pct of the fund, largest first. countries.description: From its fund file's breakdown, in percent of the fund: us_pct, the United States; weights, up to six countries, largest first, each with its ISO code (country), name and pct; and other_pct, the rest. Null as mega_cap_tech_pct is.

not_measured.description: Why a figure is null, by figure: overlap, correlation, down_weeks or profile. Absent when every figure is given.

rank.description: Its place in the order of ranking, from 1.

holders_sec_nport.description: The SEC-layer funds that hold it, heaviest first, as [fund ticker, weight percent, the quarter end the filing describes]. They are months older than holders, so they are kept apart. A fund whose row under this ticker is a foreign company's local code is not listed. A filing names a security by its ISIN, which does not say where the fund bought it. So shares that trade in New York and abroad on one ISIN (AstraZeneca, TotalEnergies, Ferrari) are listed here for the funds whose stocks are mostly on US ISINs, and under the line abroad (AZN.GB) for the others. A preferred share is keyed by its issuer's common ticker, as the filings key it, so a preferred stock fund can appear here. For a stock whose weekly is empty, a row can be dated before its first close in the price data. Such a row can be another security that had the ticker, or the company's shares abroad before it listed in New York, and etf_ownership does not count it (before_first_close).

left_out.description: An empty list for a stock with a page, and null without one; kept for compatibility. Before lines listed abroad were keyed with their market (7203.JP), it named the issuer-layer funds whose row under the ticker was most likely a company listed abroad under the same code. Today a row stays under a US ticker when its issuer's file places it in New York, by its exchange, its currency or its identifiers, with the US list for a line nothing else places. The Toronto line of the same shares as a New York line also stays under the US ticker (RY). A row in dollars that nothing places abroad counts as a US line, as a few depositary receipts traded in London do (SBID, the GDR of State Bank of India).

same_code_abroad.description: The lines listed outside the United States under the same local code, as [key, company name], most widely held first. Each is another security, and often another company: SAN.ES is Banco Santander in Madrid and SAN.FR Sanofi in Paris, beside SAN, the Santander ADR. Their issuer-layer holders are under those keys in the holders index. Their SEC-layer holders are in holders_sec_nport of the shard of their first character (/api/v1/holders/a.json for AZN.GB). An empty list when there is none.

CCO, Clear Channel Outdoor, was also Cameco's Toronto code, so it reads as CCO and CCJ; SAN reads as SAN, SAN.ES and SAN.FR. The same list as the aliases of the holders index. Null when the ticker was only ever this line.
